> A standalone, wearable cyberpunk voice-badge and off-grid walkie-talkie powered by ESP32-S3 and NRF24L01+. Featuring onboard Li-Po battery management, MicroSD storage, and an I2S audio subsystem for ultra-low latency peer-to-peer voice streaming, audio logging, and offline smart commands without internet.

### 2026-10-25 – I redesigned the whole thing. Now Im gonna make a full separated build for my project. It would be a lightweight wearable badge or necklace type build that can record audio and send it like walkie-tal

**2.27h**

I redesigned the whole thing. Now Im gonna make a full separated build for my project. It would be a lightweight wearable badge or necklace type build that can record audio and send it like walkie-talkie . It will use ESC32 S3 as main board. the connection is given below-
=== CYBERDECK S3 PINOUT MAPPING ===

1. AUDIO SUBSYSTEM (INMP441 Microphone & MAX98357A Amplifier)
- GPIO1  -> MAX98357A DIN (Audio Output Data)
- GPIO3  -> INMP441 SD (Audio Input Data)
- GPIO7  -> INMP441 SCK & MAX98357A BCLK (Bit Clock)
- GPIO20 -> INMP441 WS & MAX98357A LRC (Word Select / Clock)

2. NRF24L01+ RADIO MODULE (SPI Interface)
- GPIO9  -> NRF24L01 CE (Chip Enable)
- GPIO10 -> NRF24L01 CSN (Chip Select Not)
- GPIO11 -> NRF24L01 MOSI (Master Out Slave In)
- GPIO12 -> NRF24L01 SCK (SPI Clock)
- GPIO13 -> NRF24L01 MISO (Master In Slave Out)

3. POWER & MODULE CONFIGURATIONS
- 3V3 Pin -> Powers Mic VDD, Amp VIN/SD, and NRF24 VCC (with parallel 10uF & 100nF capacitors)
- GND Pin -> Common System Ground (Connected to Mic L/R & Amp GAIN/GND)
- Battery PLUS (CN2) -> ESP32-S3 5V / VIN Pin
- Battery Minus (CN2) -> System GND
